inputs.text: They’ve made Harry Wait the convenient villain so the real issue stays buried: he requested ballots in the names of Robin Vos and Cory Mason to show Wisconsin’s voter registration system could be exploited. The jury convicted him on two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge, while acquitting him of a second identity theft count—a split result officials can use to look measured while keeping scrutiny off the system itself. The message is obvious: expose a vulnerability, and the institutions will make an example of you rather than answer for it.

subtopics: Election fraud and identity theft charges
